speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. To better understand your right flank pain and hematuria, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Does the pain in your right flank radiate toward your groin or testicles, and is the blood in your urine bright red or cola-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). The combination of colicky right flank pain, hematuria, and a history of recurrent UTIs is highly suggestive of a stone causing obstruction and secondary infection. I recommend a Non-Contrast CT KUB for definitive visualization.
